notes:
Summary: Palisade is a fast-growing ecommerce platform (payments + marketplace) evaluating Redwood to automate contact-center workflows and perform safe tool-calls into their ticketing/refund systems. Primary goals: reduce AHT, automate refunds for simple cases, reliable escalations, and keep strict audit trail.

Key quotes: "If we can't guarantee idempotent refunds and an immutable audit trail, compliance will block the project" — VP Support (Leah Martins).

Technical context: currently using Zendesk for ticketing + an internal refund-service with REST endpoints (refund-service.company.internal). They want Redwood to: create/update tickets, call refund APIs with two-step confirmation, post back to ticket with transaction id, and optionally kick off escalation workflows in ServiceNow. Spike tolerance is critical (holiday peaks 8-12x baseline). Target SLOs: ticket update p95 < 200ms, refund call end-to-end < 800ms (including third-party payment system).

Security/compliance: must pass SOC2 + internal security checklist; data residency for EU customers; SSO (SAML) + SCIM for agents; KMS integration for key management; full request/response auditing stored for 1 year.

POC ask: sample playbook for 'refund after IVR verification', demo of tool-calling idempotency and retries, whitepaper on failure modes during spikes, cost model for dedicated GPU pool vs hosted with burst.

Internal politics: Support org and Payments team will gate behavior. Legal needs data residency confirmation. FINOPS wants ROI for dedicated commit. Platform team will own VPC peering and firewall rules.

Short notes / shorthand:
- interested in hosted for POC, want dedicated/private for production
- must show rollback semantics or compensating actions on partial failures
- JIRA INFRA-4521 open for VPC peering; legal reviewing SOW (drive link).
- demo scheduled 2026-03-15 w/ infra + payments (Priya leading).
